strengths: Novel Stackelberg game formulation that elegantly motivates asymmetric learning between representation and value learning
Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple algorithms (DQN, DDQN, Dueling variants, R2D2, PQN) and environments with 30 seeds per experiment and proper statistical analysis
Thorough ablation studies demonstrating importance of all three design choices: follower objective, role assignment, and hierarchical coupling
Practical implementation requiring only learning rate modifications with demonstrated imperceptible computational overhead
Strong and consistent empirical improvements including dramatic gains on Breakout (3x DQN score) and solving hard exploration tasks (Four Rooms)
Extends beyond replay-based methods to recurrent networks and online learning, demonstrating generality
Convergence analysis provided with explicit characterization in terms of network architecture parameters
weaknesses: Significant theory-practice gap: convergence analysis proves optimization convergence, not sample complexity improvements that empirically occur; no theoretical explanation for why Bellman error variance minimization reduces sample complexity
Scope severely limited to discrete action spaces; all experiments restricted to this setting while continuous control is standard in modern deep RL
Follower's variance objective (Eq. 2) lacks theoretical justification; computed on current batch raises potential circularity concerns; why this specific objective over alternatives?

Architecture separation is an unexamined design choice; monolithic baseline is the split network trained uniformly, not independently optimized; unclear if gains come from game dynamics or architectural separation itself

Incomplete comparison with related approaches: excludes auxiliary losses and self-supervised learning without exploring these alternatives; missing comparisons with recent stabilization methods and state-of-the-art baselines
Limited characterization of when SCORER helps most; no analysis of problem properties that benefit from the framework; unclear why Breakout shows largest improvements
Hyperparameter sensitivity not thoroughly explored; critical learning rate ratio αϕ/αθ may be difficult for practitioners to set in new domains
Gap between theory (assumes convergence to best response) and practice (one-step updates) insufficiently addressed despite acknowledgment
Role of target networks in interaction with two-timescale dynamics underexplored; unclear if essential or orthogonal

strengths: Novel Stackelberg game formulation for modeling representation-value coupling provides creative and well-motivated perspective on deep Q-learning instability
Practical implementation requiring only asymmetric learning rate schedules without architectural changes, facilitating adoption and fair comparison
Comprehensive and rigorous empirical evaluation across MinAtar, Atari, MinGrid, and classic control with proper statistical methodology (IQM, bootstrap CIs, 30 seeds)
Strong consistent improvements on MinAtar benchmarks (e.g., 3x gain in Breakout) across multiple base algorithms (DQN variants, R2D2, PQN)
Thorough ablation studies cleanly isolating the three key design choices and validating each component's necessity
Stability analysis demonstrating effectiveness on pathological cases (Baird's counterexample, stochastic Deep Sea)
weaknesses: Limited theoretical contributions: convergence analysis (Appendix M) applies standard two-timescale theory without deep RL-specific insights; assumptions (Lipschitz continuity, RSI, strong convexity) not rigorously justified for Bellman error variance objective; no sample complexity characterization connecting variance minimization to improved convergence rates

Bellman error variance objective lacks rigorous justification: the decomposition Var[δ]=Var_aleatoric+Var_epistemic is presented without proof; unclear why batch-level variance minimization improves value function quality; follower and leader see different batches, raising questions about proper stabilization

Unclear necessity of hierarchical Stackelberg coupling: inverted role ablation shows failure but not that game-theoretic formulation is essential; 'monolithic per-layer LR' baseline shows modest advantage; missing comparisons with alternative representation stabilization methods (e.g., decoupled learning approaches)

Mixed empirical results on high-dimensional benchmarks: Atari-5 results are modest and inconsistent (some games match baseline), limited to only 5 games rather than standard Atari-57; MiniGrid strong results only on Four Rooms

Hyperparameter tuning complexity: two-stage search with sensitivity to learning rate ratio (Figure 12 shows drops at 2:1 ratio); unclear how generalizable across domains; practical applicability requires careful domain-specific tuning

Stop-gradient operations to implement hierarchical game seem orthogonal to Stackelberg equilibrium concept and lack clear theoretical justification; design choice appears pragmatic rather than principled
